_why: Profiles are DECLARED here, never discovered by scanning a directory. A
scanner would pick up ~/.config/kipi/reddit-profile, and a Playwright
profile login for Reddit is WAF-blocked and forbidden (canon 2026-07-17,
reddit_driver.py). Declaring is what keeps a forbidden surface out.
Every entry MUST carry a liveness_probe. browser_session_health.load_profiles
refuses the whole file otherwise: a profile whose liveness cannot be checked
is not a persistent session, it is a guess.
logged_in_marker is a string that appears ONLY when signed in. It is matched
case-insensitively against the loaded page. Pick the sign-OUT control, never
the sign-in one: a page that failed to render also lacks the sign-in link.
kill_switch: touch that file and the profile is skipped entirely, no browser
opened and no alert, with no config edit and no deploy.
Adding a profile is this file plus a human sign-in. Alerting is already
per-profile (browser_session_health.run_once keys alerted_state by name), so
a second entry needs no code change.

profiles.name: research-hn
profiles.purpose: Reference profile for the persistent-browsing capability. Neutral surface with a real signed-in/signed-out distinction and a cheap page, chosen so continuity is provable without pointing this at any client target.
